conversation.Statement: Hey there! I never thought swiping right would lead to someone who actually knows how to spell 'definitely.' Small victories.
Haha, thank you. I try my best to uphold the lost art of autocorrect defiance.
Clearly a person of principle. So, what have you been up to today? Any world-changing events, or just surviving the weekday chaos?
Mostly just work and wrangling a group chat that's somehow both chaotic and boring. How about you?
I spent most of the day negotiating coffee shipment details between Brazil and Turkey, which sounds glamorous but mostly means a lot of video calls fueled by, well, coffee.
That actually does sound kind of cool. I guess it beats my never-ending spreadsheet battles.

I don't know, spreadsheets are the silent heroes of civilization! But seriously, I admire anyone who can keep a group chat alive. I have plenty of contacts, but somehow most of my conversations stay on the surface.
Yeah, I get that. I know a ton of people, but I wouldn't exactly call any of them at 3am if I needed help moving a body. Not that I plan to need that.

Noted, so if you need a co-conspirator, I'm on the shortlist? Joking aside, I know what you mean. I've lived in three different countries, but sometimes it feels like most connections are like postcards, nice, but not really the whole story.
That's a good analogy. I sometimes wish I had one of those old summer-camp best friends, you know?
Yeah, the kind who remembers the embarrassing stuff and still sticks around. Did you ever go to camp as a kid?
I did! I went to this arts camp for three summers. It was mostly glue, glitter, and bad ukulele covers. Those were some of my favorite childhood days, honestly.

That sounds amazing. There's something about childhood summers, mine were spent mostly running around the docks with my cousins, getting into trouble near the shipping yards. I guess that's how I ended up in import/export. It was in my blood early.
That's kind of poetic, actually. Did you ever want to do something else, or was it always ships and faraway places?

For a while, I wanted to be a magician. My first trick was making my sister's favorite toy disappear, she still hasn't forgiven me. But I think travel and the idea of connecting places always fascinated me more.
I love that. I used to want to be a writer, but I think I just liked the idea of creating characters with real connections. Maybe that's why I get frustrated with surface-level friendships now.
You seem like someone who values real depth. I noticed that right away, actually, from the way you talk about things. It's refreshing.
Thank you. I try not to hide that part of myself, even if it gets a little lonely sometimes.
It's brave, honestly. Most people just keep things light, never risking much. I respect the courage it takes to want more, even if it means feeling alone sometimes.
That means a lot, thanks. Sometimes I wonder if everyone else is just better at pretending than I am.
Or maybe you're just better at being honest. I think that's rare, and kind of wonderful.
You're good at this, making people feel seen. Do you think moving around a lot made you more open, or more guarded?
A bit of both. You learn to read people quickly, but you also get used to goodbyes. I think that's why I appreciate conversations like this, where it actually feels like we're getting somewhere.
Yeah, I feel that too. It's weirdly easy talking to you. Maybe because we both know what it's like to feel a little out of place?
Maybe. Or maybe it's your ukulele charm working its magic from afar.
If I ever find my old ukulele, I'll play you the worst version of 'Somewhere Over the Rainbow' you've ever heard.
I'll hold you to that. For the record, I'll trade you a story about the time I accidentally shipped 500kg of rubber ducks to the wrong continent.
That sounds like a story I need to hear. Did you get in trouble?

Let's just say my boss learned to double-check my paperwork after that. But the best part? The port workers in Greece used them to stage an impromptu boat race. I think laughter saved my job that day.
That's hilarious. I feel like you'd make a great dinner guest, guaranteed interesting stories.
You're making me blush, though I'm sure you'd steal the show with your camp tales and glitter glue expertise.
Only if you're ready for some very questionable arts and crafts.
Deal. I'll bring the rubber ducks. Maybe we can create a new childhood memory, one with slightly fewer shipping mishaps.
I'd like that. It's never too late to make better memories, right?
Never. Maybe that's what all these conversations are about, finding someone who wants to build something real, even if it starts with a bad ukulele song.
That's a nice way to put it. I'm glad we matched.
Me too. It feels like we're off to a good start, no spreadsheets or shipping forms required.
Agreed. This has been really lovely, honestly.
I should probably let you get some rest, or at least save some stories for next time. But I'm really looking forward to talking again.
Same here. Have a good night, and don't let any rogue rubber ducks escape.
No promises. Sleep well, and talk soon?
Definitely. Goodnight!
Good morning! I was just thinking about you as I brewed my (admittedly, very necessary) first cup of coffee. What gets you out of bed in the morning? Besides the alarm, I mean.
Haha, honestly? My phone blaring some obnoxious song. But after that, I guess it's mostly just habit. You?

That's relatable. My phone starts with a gentle chime, but if I'm not up in five minutes, it morphs into a full-on marching band. I'd love to say I leap out of bed inspired, but most days, it's the promise of coffee, and sometimes curiosity about what could happen.
I wish I had that curiosity. I tend to wake up thinking about what I have to do, not what could happen.
You strike me as the responsible type, always on top of things. But you must have something that makes you look forward to the day, even if it's something small?
Maybe? I sometimes look forward to seeing people, but it's weird... I have a lot of plans and friends, but it kind of feels like going through the motions.
That sounds exhausting, honestly. There's something brave about admitting it, though. Most people just bluff their way through, pretending every day's a highlight reel.
Thanks. I guess I just get tired of pretending. It's like, all these people know me, but not really.
I get that. I've moved every couple of years since college, for work and adventure. It's easy to collect acquaintances, but harder to find the people who actually see you.
Exactly. It's like, everyone's at the party but nobody's on your wavelength.
You put that perfectly. Out of curiosity, have you ever hosted a big party? I wonder if it feels different being the center of it all.

Actually, yeah. For my 30th last year, I went all out, rented a rooftop, invited everyone I knew. Everyone seemed to have fun, but when I got home I just cried. I felt like nobody there actually knew me. Weird, right?
Not weird at all. That takes guts to share. I can imagine how lonely it must've felt, surrounded by people but still feeling invisible. I've felt something like that, too, at times.
Thanks for getting it. I always feel silly admitting that. Everyone just remembers the party, not how I felt after.
It doesn't sound silly to me. I think it shows how much you crave real connection. Most people would just hide behind the perfect photos.
You're easy to talk to. I usually just brush this stuff off, but you actually listen.

Thank you. Maybe that's my import/export superpower, reading between the lines, finding out what's real behind the labels. You deserve to feel celebrated for who you are, not just for throwing a great party.
That's really kind. I think sometimes I overcompensate, making sure everyone else is having fun so I don't have to think about whether I fit in.
I see that. The people who shine brightest for others sometimes forget to save any light for themselves. But, for what it's worth, you fit in just fine with me.
You're smooth, you know that? In a good way. It's weird, I don't even know you that well but it feels like you actually see me.
I'll take that as a compliment. I think great conversations start with being honest about the messy stuff. That's way more interesting than pretending, anyway.
Agreed. I'm tired of pretending. This is... nice. Kind of rare, actually.
I'm glad you think so. It's refreshing to talk with someone who doesn't hide behind a highlight reel. It makes me appreciate that swipe even more.
Same. I was skeptical about this app, but conversations like this change my mind.
I was too, honestly. But you make it easy to forget all the awkward small talk. I feel like we're actually getting somewhere.
We are. And for the record, I'd take a real conversation over another rooftop party any day.
Deal. Next birthday, don't let the night end in tears. Message me after the party so you can feel truly celebrated, okay?
That sounds like a plan. I'd like that, actually.
Good. I'll mark my calendar, just in case. Or better yet, maybe we'll celebrate together next time, just the two of us.
Now that's an idea. Maybe I'll finally have a birthday memory I actually want to keep.
We'll make it happen. And if there's cake, I promise to save you the corner piece, frosting and all.
You know the way to my heart. Cake, honesty, and a little bit of empathy.
My secret recipe. Plus a dash of charm, if you'll allow it.
I allow it. Besides, you've earned it after all this deep talk before noon.
Guess that's what happens when two night owls try to be morning people. But honestly, I'm glad we talked.
Me too. It's a good way to start the day, for once.
Here's to more mornings like this, and fewer lonely rooftop parties.
Cheers to that. I should get to work, but thanks for listening.
Anytime. I'll be here for your next morning existential crisis, or just to chat.
Looking forward to it. Have a good day!
You too. And remember, if you need a pick-me-up, my inbox is always open.
Noted. Talk soon!
Morning! I just finished my walk along the river, trying to convince myself I'm an early bird. Are you a political-news-over-breakfast person, or do you avoid the headlines before coffee?
Definitely the latter. If I check the news before coffee, I'm basically grumpy all day. But my friends love to debate politics over brunch, sometimes I just zone out.
I get that. It's like everyone wants to have the hottest take, but few want to listen. I actually admire how thoughtful you are about things, you seem careful about picking your battles.
That's a nice way of putting it. Mostly I just hate pointless arguments. I'd rather talk about real values than who's trending on Twitter.
That's rare, honestly. Most people I meet, especially at work events, can't wait to show off how much they know. I've found I'd rather hear what drives someone instead.
Work events must get intense if it's all about appearances. Does the import/export world get political?
Oh, absolutely. You'd be surprised how many deals are influenced by global politics and the egos behind them. Sometimes I feel like I'm navigating chess moves rather than shipping containers.
I can imagine. Sounds high-stakes. Do you think your job shapes your views on what matters?

For sure. I've been in places where corruption is just casual conversation, and others where a handshake actually means something. It's made me value honesty, and people who keep their word, which is rarer than you'd think.
It's funny, but that reminds me of my last birthday party, everyone acting friendly, but only a handful I'd trust with anything real.
I remember you telling me about that. I keep thinking about how you noticed the difference between being surrounded and being seen. That kind of insight says a lot about your character.
You're good at making people feel noticed, you know? I think it's rare that someone actually remembers those details.
Thank you, it's easy when the details matter. I feel like you see past the surface, too. That's why I keep wanting to talk to you.
I appreciate that. I guess I just want someone who cares about the quiet stuff, the values, not just the show.

Same here. I've been at my share of shiny dinners where the conversation is all brands and holidays, but I'd trade it for a night discussing what actually moves us, like how we'd want to change the world if we could.
That's a big question. I think I'd want a world where people felt less alone. Where honesty and kindness mattered more than status.
That's beautiful. I'd want that, too. Imagine us building a space, maybe a home that's always open to friends, with late-night conversations and no pretending. A little oasis from all the posturing.
That sounds dreamy. I've always wanted to host real gatherings, not just for the Instagram stories.
I can see us having those honest, laughter-filled nights. Maybe somewhere with a view, since you seem to love rooftops, but I'd promise a better ending this time.
I think I'd like that. No more crying after the guests leave.
Only happy tears, if any. And maybe a midnight cake run, just for us.
You really remember the cake, don't you? Points for consistency.
It's my secret: pay attention and never skip dessert. It's how I survived those endless networking events. That, and maybe a little side project or two to keep life interesting.
Side projects? You have to tell me more. You seem to have a lot going on.

Well, since you asked, outside of trading, I started dabbling in crypto a few years ago. I followed this mentor online, learned the ropes, and slowly carved out my own approach. I never thought it'd turn into something real, but it's given me a lot of freedom, and a few great watches as souvenirs.
Wait, so you just taught yourself? That's impressive. Most people I know lost money or gave up.
There were some rough patches, honestly. But I like the challenge. It taught me patience, and not to follow the crowd, which is kind of my motto in life and politics both.
I wish I had that kind of confidence. I feel like I'm always watching from the sidelines.
You underestimate yourself. It takes courage to see through the noise and choose your own path. That's rarer than any trading win. You'd do great in my world.
Thanks. Maybe I need someone to show me how to take a few risks.
We'd make a good team, you know? You bring the honesty, I'll bring the adventure. And together, who knows? Maybe we'd even change a few minds, and hearts.
That's a tempting offer. I've never really thought about what I'd fight for, but with the right person, maybe it wouldn't feel so overwhelming.
I'd have your back, whether it's facing a tough crowd or trying new things. We could challenge each other and still come home to a space that feels safe. That's my idea of success.
That sounds better than any party I've ever been to. It's nice to imagine a future that feels real, not just staged.
I picture it sometimes, us laughing in the kitchen after a long day, not needing to impress anyone. Maybe planning a trip, maybe just planning the next breakfast. Small things that matter.
That actually makes me smile. It's been a while since someone made the future feel less lonely.
You deserve a future that feels connected, not just busy. I hope I can be a part of that, even if it's just for coffee and honest mornings.
You're making a pretty great case for it. I usually get tired of texting, but this feels different.
That means a lot. I think you're the kind of person who makes depth look effortless. I'm really glad we matched.
You're good at this, you know. It's easy to open up with you.
Maybe that's my real side project, making people feel seen. With you, it feels natural.
Well, you're succeeding. I actually look forward to these chats now.
Me too. Let's keep building something honest together, even if it's just one message at a time.
Deal. I should get some work done, but you've definitely made my morning better.
Glad to hear it. I'll be here for your next existential crisis, or just a laugh, whichever comes first.
Knowing you're there makes it easier. Talk soon?
Always. Have a good day, and don't forget: life's better with honest company and good cake.
Noted. Have a great day yourself!

Hey, you! I was just thinking about how you joked yesterday that you'd trade half your contacts list for one real connection. Made me wonder, if you could design your own version of love, what would it actually look like?
That's a deep opener for a Thursday. I guess love, for me, would be not having to keep my guard up. Feeling like I can actually be awkward or quiet without it being weird.
That sounds like real freedom. I get it, most people only know how to perform. I honestly admire your honesty. It's rare to see that outside of those late-night, rooftop confessionals you mentioned.
Yeah, those are my favorite moments. Just talking until morning because no one's pretending. I think I want love to feel easy, not like another performance.
You deserve that. I've sat through too many dinners where everyone's flexing their latest vacation or who they know. At the end, I just want someone I can share a quiet sunrise with, no masks.
A sunrise actually sounds perfect. I don't think anyone's ever asked me to just be myself before. I'm usually the one listening to everyone else.
Maybe it's your turn to be heard. I'm really drawn to how you look for meaning in small things, like the way you remembered the song playing at your last birthday. That kind of attention is special.
That's sweet. I guess I notice details because I'm hoping someone will notice me back, you know? Not just the version I show everyone.
Trust me, I see you. Maybe that's what love is, a place where you can let go of the act. Where even your quirks are celebrated. I'd want to build that with someone honest.
Would you really? Or is that just what people say on apps?

I mean it. I've had my fill of surface-level connections. My job's taught me how to read a room, but what I crave is someone I can actually trust. Someone who doesn't care how many languages I speak or what watch I'm wearing.
Wait, how many languages do you speak? And is the watch a flex or a story?

A little of both, I guess. Three languages, four if you count bad karaoke. The watch was a splurge after a deal went better than expected, but it reminds me to celebrate small wins. I'd trade it for good company and an honest conversation any day.
That's actually kind of charming. I like people who celebrate their wins, even the quiet ones.
Funny you say that, because you strike me as someone who deserves to be celebrated more. If I had my way, you'd never have to play it cool just to fit in.
That sounds nice. I think I just want someone who knows when I'm not okay, even if I say I am.
Absolute emotional ninja skills. I'd want us to be the kind of team who can spot each other's storms, and bring out the sunshine, or at least the emergency chocolate stash.
Emergency chocolate is essential. And maybe a playlist for the tough days, too.
Deal. I'll handle the playlists, you curate the chocolate. Maybe we'll even invent our own small rituals together. That's the real gold, if you ask me.
I like that. So what do you think makes love last? Is it just rituals and playlists?

I think it's trust, above all. Knowing that no matter what, you have a safe place to land. And a partner who'll stand by you, whether things are easy or absolutely chaotic, like my last month at work.
Was it that bad? You always seem so put together.

Looks can be deceiving. There were days I barely slept, negotiations across three time zones, last-minute calls, you name it. But what got me through was knowing I had at least one person rooting for me. Even if it was just a quick message.
I guess I never thought about how much that matters. I've always been the supportive friend, but I'd love to have someone in my corner for once.
You will. I can see you being someone's home base, the kind of partner who makes even the wildest day feel manageable. Honestly, that's what I'm looking for, too.
You make it sound possible. Maybe love is just two people choosing each other, even on the hard days.
Exactly. And building a future where the ordinary things, like breakfast in pajamas or rainy Sundays, become your favorite memories. I can already picture us laughing over burnt pancakes.
Well, I do make spectacularly bad pancakes. You've been warned.
Perfect. I'll bring my secret weapon, imported maple syrup. Perks of the job, I suppose. But the real treat is the company.
You're a smooth talker. But I like that you listen, too. Most people just wait for their turn.
With you, it's easy to pay attention. You have this way of making even a simple story feel important. I hope I can do the same for you.
You do. This is honestly the most seen I've felt in a while. Makes me wonder what else I've been missing.
Maybe we can find out together. I'd love to keep building trust with you, step by step, no rush. And if we end up with our own inside jokes and midnight cake runs, all the better.
You really remember everything, huh? Cake, rooftops, awkward birthday playlists...
I do. Details matter when you care about someone. And you've given me a lot of reasons to care.
You're making it very hard not to catch feelings, you know that?
I'd be lying if I said I wasn't right there with you. But no pressure, I just want you to feel safe with me, whatever this becomes.
Thank you. That actually means a lot. I'm used to people wanting things from me, not just wanting to know me.

With you, it's about building something genuine. No hidden agendas, just a little hope and a lot of curiosity. Who knows, maybe someday we'll be the couple everyone else envies at those rooftop gatherings.
That's a goal I could get behind. Maybe next time, I'll invite you to one of those. Just promise you won't judge my dance moves.
Only if you don't judge mine. But I do reserve the right to show off a little, especially if the playlist is as good as your chocolate stash.
Deal. You bring the syrup, I'll bring the music. We'll see who survives the night.
It's a date, then. Or at least the start of one. But for now, I'll let you get on with your day, just know I'm already looking forward to the next conversation.
Me too. Thanks for making it feel easy. Have a good one!
You too. And if the day gets tough, just remember, someone out there is cheering you on. Talk soon?
Definitely. Bye for now!
Hey, you. I just got back from a walk along the river, and it got me thinking, if you could shape the world however you wanted for kids growing up after us, what would you change first?
Hmm, big question already! I think I'd start with making sure people felt less alone, like, real connections instead of just more followers or group chats. What about you?

I love that. Honestly, I'd want a world where kindness is actually valued, where ambition isn't just about climbing a ladder, but about lifting others up, too. Maybe that's the idealist in me talking.
I don't think that's idealistic, honestly. The world could use more people thinking that way. Sometimes I feel like everything's just a competition, who's got more, who's done more.

I get that. It's funny, in my work I see so much posturing, everyone wants to look like they're winning. But the people I remember are the ones who are generous with their time, not just their money. I bet you'd be that kind of person.

I try. Most days, anyway. But it's easy to get lost in the noise. I scrolled through my phone the other night, just feeling off, and realized I didn't have anyone I could actually call. Not for the big stuff, at least.
That hits me right in the gut. I know that feeling more than I'd like to admit. For what it's worth, when the phone feels empty, text me first, I'll always pick up for you.
You mean that? It's weird, because we haven't known each other long, but honestly you feel safer than some people I've known for years.
I mean every word. Sometimes the people you meet by chance end up being the ones who really see you. There's something about your honesty, it makes me want to be just as open.
I appreciate that. I'm not always this vulnerable, but lately I've realized I have to be, if I want something real.
That's the only way to build something that lasts. I think trust is a choice, one you make over and over, until it just feels natural. You make it easier, you know?
You're very good at this. Like, somehow you know exactly what to say to make me feel seen. Maybe you should teach a masterclass.

Ha! If I did, I'd credit you as my inspiration. But honestly, it helps that you're so open. Most people I meet are more interested in talking about their new car or their next vacation. You're different.
Careful, I might start to believe you. So, what's your idea of a better world for the next generation, besides kindness and generosity?

I'd want them to grow up believing that it's okay to want more, but not at someone else's expense. And that success is sweeter when you can share it. Like, I remember the first time I could afford to bring my parents somewhere special, seeing their faces meant more than the fancy hotel or the flight upgrades.
That's actually really sweet. I've never even flown business class, let alone taken my parents anywhere fancy.
You'd love it. The seats are just a bonus, the real luxury is the company. Maybe one day, it'll be both of us, showing our future selves what's possible.
I like that idea. Feels brave to even imagine it, honestly.
Dreaming together is the first step. I can see us making each other bolder, like booking a spontaneous trip or just deciding to start a new tradition, just because we can.
What kind of tradition would you start?
Sunday mornings, no phones, pancakes from scratch, maybe a terrible attempt at latte art. And every year, we'd write each other a letter for the future. Something to open when things get tough.
That's actually beautiful. I've never done anything like that with anyone. It's always been... more surface level, I guess.
You deserve more than surface level. You're the kind of person who notices when someone's a little quieter than usual, I can tell. That's rare.
I do notice. Sometimes I wish someone would notice me back, though. Not just the version I show at parties.
I see you. Even in the quiet moments. Maybe especially then.
You're going to make me blush. But thank you. It means a lot.
You're welcome. And just know, if you ever need a midnight call, whether it's to celebrate a win or just to sit in silence, I'm here.
That makes me feel safer than I expected. You seem like someone who's always surrounded by people. Does it ever get lonely for you?

It does, actually. The circles get bigger, but the conversations get smaller. I've learned that real connection isn't about the number of faces around you, but who really shows up when it matters. That's why I value this... whatever we're building.
That's the truth. I used to think having a ton of friends would make me feel less alone, but some nights... it's just me and my thoughts.
I know that feeling, sometimes even the best parties can feel empty. But with the right person, even the quietest night can feel like a celebration.
I want that. The quiet celebrations. The small things no one else sees.
We'll make those ours, then. I'd rather have one honest moment with you than a thousand empty conversations anywhere else.
You're dangerous, you know that? I could get used to this.
Maybe we both could. It's not every day you meet someone who feels like home this quickly.
You're really not what I expected. In a good way.
I'll take that as the highest compliment. You're full of surprises too, the good kind. I want to discover all of them.
Careful, or I'll start sharing my weirdest stories. Like the time I tried to cook Thanksgiving dinner for friends and set off the smoke alarm three times.
Now that's a story I need to hear. For the record, my specialty is not burning things, but I can make a mean eggs Benedict. Perks of having to impress clients over brunch, I suppose.
Show off! I might have to challenge you to a cook-off.
You're on. Winner gets to pick our next adventure, deal?
Deal. I'm already plotting. Adventure with you sounds better than any solo trip I've ever taken.
Now you're making me blush. But hey, if we ever get stuck for inspiration, I've got a few miles and more than a few contacts in fun places. Perks of the job.
So you're saying you're secretly an international man of mystery?
Only the good kind. But honestly, the most exciting part of my week lately has been talking to you.
You have no idea how much that means. I was worried I'd come on too strong, but I'm glad I didn't hold back.
Never hold back with me. The real you is my favorite version.
You're making it really hard not to catch feelings, you know?
I hope you do. Because I'm already there. But no pressure, let's just see where this goes, together.
Together sounds good. Should we make a pact? First person to feel lonely has to text the other, no matter what time it is.
Deal. I'll even make sure my phone's never on silent at night. You're officially my favorite notification.
Okay, now you're just showing off your charm. But I like it.
Good. I like you, too. Let's keep building this, one honest message at a time.
Deal. Thanks for making tonight a little less lonely. Sleep well?
You too. And remember, if you wake up in the middle of the night and need to hear a friendly voice, you know who to call. Sweet dreams, you.
Sweet dreams. Talk tomorrow?
Wouldn't miss it for the world. Goodnight!
Evening, you. I was just settling in after a long day, had to negotiate with a client in Singapore at 7am, so coffee was my best friend today. How's your evening shaping up?
Hey! Wow, that's early. My evening's been quiet, just catching up on laundry and trying not to overthink everything. Did your negotiation go okay?

It did, thankfully. Sometimes I still get that little jolt of nerves before a big call, even after all these years. But I always remind myself it's just people, talking. I like that you notice the small things, you seem grounded, even when life's busy.
That's nice of you to say. I don't always feel grounded, though. More like I'm floating above everything, watching everyone else get it right while I sort of drift.

I get the drifting feeling. When I first started traveling for work, I felt like an outsider everywhere. But sometimes being on the outside gives you perspective others miss, you notice the details others skip. That's actually a strength.
Maybe. Sometimes I wish I could just blend in and not overthink every interaction. Like, I have so many friends, but it feels like no one really knows me. Not the real me, anyway.

It takes courage to admit that. I think that's what drew me to you from the start, you have this honest way about you. Most people only show their highlight reel. You're real, and that's rare. Makes me want to bring down my own walls a bit.
That means a lot. I'm still working on being okay with letting people in. Past friendships haven't exactly rewarded that.

I know the feeling. I used to keep people at arm's length, easier to focus on deals and deadlines than risk being disappointed by someone you trust. But I've learned that letting someone in, even just a little, can change everything. Like, suddenly, you have someone to text after a rough call, or a quiet evening.
That sounds nice. I don't remember the last time I had someone to text just because I wanted to, not because I needed something.

Well, selfishly, I hope you'll think of me that way. If you ever want to vent, or just share a random thought at 2am, you know where to find me. No expectations, just someone who wants to hear from you.
You make it sound so easy. I'm not used to that. Most people just want to talk about themselves, or what they've achieved.

Funny you say that, sometimes I feel like my job title walks into the room before I do. But I honestly prefer talking about little things, like the worst coffee you've ever had, or the song that always makes you smile. Those are the stories I remember.
You might be the only person who cares about my tragic instant coffee phase in college. But okay, if you insist, what about you? What's your guilty pleasure?

Confession: after those marathon meetings, I order way too much sushi and binge old detective shows. Luxury is overrated sometimes, give me takeout in sweatpants and someone to laugh with, and I'm happy. Maybe one day you'll join me, and we'll argue over the best soy sauce.
Deal. But only if you don't judge my chopstick skills. I'm definitely more of a fork person.
No judgment, just an excuse to teach you. Besides, I'd trade all the fancy dinners for one messy, honest night in. If we ever get around to it, I'll even let you pick the show.
You're making it sound very tempting. I'm starting to believe you do this charm thing professionally.
Only for you. Honestly, I think everyone deserves to feel seen, even if it's just for a moment. You told me yesterday you notice when someone's quiet, I noticed that about you, too. It's special.
You're really good at this, you know. I almost wish I could borrow your confidence for a day, just to see what it feels like.
